text:
ashok_infra: heads-up: APNE1 rack pn-03 showing mixed Xid 13 / 79 / 48 across several A10 and A30 cards, started ~2026-03-19 21:00 UTC. correlates with tenant b-kk small-batch burst. noticed ECC counts tick up on two cards.

maria_sre: oof. any recent infra changes? kernel/driver/runtime rollouts?

ashok_infra: quick paste of what I grabbed from node pn-03-12:
```
$ nvidia-smi -q -d ECC
GPU 0: A10
  ECC Errors (Volatile): 13
  ECC Errors (Aggregate): 120
GPU 1: A30
  ECC Errors (Volatile): 2
  ECC Errors (Aggregate): 4

$ dmesg | tail -n50
[3421123.123] NVRM: Xid (13) at 0xFFFF: PID 4123: /opt/redwood/runtime/bin/serve (decode)
[3421123.124] NVRM: Xid (79) GPU 0000:3b:00.0: Call timed out during VA op
[3421150.456] NVRM: Xid (48) - ECC multi-bit detected on GPU 0
```

lee_runtime: we rolled continuous-batching default to 1.2.3 at 20:30 UTC for apne1. that increases small-batch concurrency and prefix caching. could amplify KV cache pressure and small-token loops.

tim_gpuops: pulled telemetry: small-batch % (<=8 tokens) jumped from 12% -> 48% for tenant b-kk at 21:00. co-occurring: per-card inflight ctx count doubled, NIC rx_errors up on those hosts. snippet: 
```
# eth0 stats (pn-03-12)
rx_errors: 312
rx_dropped: 45
tx_errors: 0
```

deploy-bot: deploy "runtime/continuous-batching@1.2.3" completed by lee_runtime at 2026-03-19T20:30:07Z :rocket:

jess_customer_success: are customers seeing 5xx or just latency blips? which tenants affected?

ashok_infra: two tenants reported elevated 5xx (b-kk and c-ll). b-kk highest error rate ~3% during the burst window. errors are GPU-side decode failures returning 13/79.

maria_sre: hypothesis so far: new batching increases occupancy on certain cards w/ slightly aged firmware/driver combo -> ECC exposes multi-bit (Xid48) and then kernel/runtime triggers Xid13/79 during VA/decoder ops. also NIC drops increase causes retries and tighter scheduling, raising contention.

lee_runtime: can we repro locally by simulating high small-batch concurrency against A10 with current driver? I can spin up a test pod and run the embedder workload. need node access and the exact runtime flags used.

ashok_infra: I'll snapshot node: driver version 535.86, CUDA 12.2, firmware v4.6. Also saw one card with rising temperature + ECC single->multi flip.

tim_gpuops: mitigation options:
- soft-drain pn-03-12 and pn-03-14 (evict non-critical tenants)
- roll runtime back to 1.2.2 for APNE1 until we validate
- temporarily cap per-card concurrency for small-batch requests (runtime flag)
- file vendor ticket for firmware/driver combination re: Xid48 -> 13 cascade

maria_sre: agree. immediate: soft-drain the two most noisy nodes, move high QPS tenants to other racks. medium: cap concurrency + revert if necessary. long: vendor escalation + upgrade firmware after maintenance window.

lee_runtime: I'll prepare a repro job and a runtime toggle: `--max-small-batch-concurrency=4` for apne1. can we patch prod config quickly?

ashok_infra: doing soft-drain now for pn-03-12: `redwood-cli node soft-drain pn-03-12 --reason "Xid spike apne1" --timeout 30m`

ashok_infra: also created ticket INFRA-4521 to collect: dmesg, nvidia-smi -q, firmware, perf counters, and tenant traces. tagging vendor.

jess_customer_success: i'll ping the two affected customers with a short note (we're investigating, may route requests).

tim_gpuops: follow-up: please collect `nvidia-smi nvlink -q` and `pci-stats` from those hosts. NVLINK errors were correlated in past to Xid79 on multi-gpu decode ops.

maria_sre: i'll own the rollback plan if runtime toggle doesn't help. thanks everyone. I'll update this thread with drain status and vendor response. :thumbsup:
